name: kimi-k3-in-c
works_with: Linux x86-64, macOS arm64 and Windows x86-64
short: Runs the 2.78 trillion parameter Kimi K3 model on one CPU with as little as 8 GB of RAM, in plain C99 with no GPU.
what: A Kimi K3 inference engine in portable C99, with no BLAS, framework or GPU. It streams the model from disk, so 8 GB of RAM works and more memory only makes it faster. The README measures 26.5 seconds per token on 8 GB and 5.6 seconds on 128 GB or more, with the same output at every size. A test suite checks the engine against a PyTorch reference without downloading the model.
who: People interested in how a huge model can run on ordinary hardware. It is slow, and the checkpoint is 1.56 TB, so skip it if you want a usable chat model.
needs: About 1.7 TB of free disk, ideally fast local storage
A CPU with AVX2 and FMA (x86-64) or NEON (arm64)
GCC 9+ or Clang 10+, with GNU make or CMake
Python 3.9+ for the download and pack tools

steps.title: Clone, build and test
steps.text: This needs no checkpoint, network or Python, and takes about a minute.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c.git
cd kimi-k3-in-c

make -j            # seconds. Seven C files, a compiler and OpenMP
make test          # under a minute

steps.title: Check your machine
steps.text: It checks the toolchain, sizes your RAM to a preset, measures your disk and prints the next command.

steps.title: Download the checkpoint
steps.text: 1.56 TB, so this takes hours. It is resumable, and it verifies every shard at the end.
steps.code:
export HF_TOKEN=hf_your_token_here          # read from the environment, never echoed
./scripts/download-model.sh ~/k3model       # resumable, re-run to continue

steps.title: Pack the trunk
steps.text: About four minutes, once. It writes a 109 GB file, so put it on your fastest disk.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Before downloading anything, run `make test`. It should end with ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY and ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED.

watch: The checkpoint is 1.56 TB plus a 109 GB packed file. The download takes hours.
A partial download produces wrong tokens without failing loudly. Treat a FAIL from the verify step as a stop.
It is slow: the README measures 26.5 seconds per token on 8 GB of RAM. The first token of a run also loads every pinned layer from disk.
Pick a preset that matches your RAM. `./bin/k3 --list-presets` shows them.
